Subject: Redlines on MSA - operator liability & forensics exhibit

Marissa,

Thanks for the MSA and order form — we ran it by Legal & Security and have three items that need clearer language for us to sign for an on-prem / VPC deployment:

1) Forensics & chain-of-custody: we need explicit language describing how a forensic snapshot is collected, who can witness it, and what constitutes acceptable cryptographic proof of provenance. We attached a redline that inserts an "Exhibit: Forensics & Evidence" with options A/B.

2) Operator rights vs. entitlements: Meridian requires operator access to be strictly scoped (read-only debug console + ephemeral witness sessions). We can't accept broad "operator access" that permits pull of customer data without controls. Please clarify fallback and escalation routes in cases of subpoena/forensic request.

3) Audit window / witnessing: We prefer certified snapshot delivery (encrypted snapshot + HSM-signed manifest) or a witness-on-site option. If neither is feasible, we need a short SLA for turnaround and a guarantee of an audit log export for the forensic window.

Can we schedule a short alignment call tomorrow? I've attached our redlines and a suggested forensics clause.

Thanks,
Priya Nair

Priya / Marissa —

Thanks — I reviewed the redline and here are concrete counter-proposals inline. I pasted the relevant snippets below and attached a tracked version for ease: MSA_redlines_Meridian_20260824.docx (tracked).

1) Forensics & chain-of-custody (new Exhibit X):
Proposed compromise language (short form):
"Exhibit X (Forensics & Evidence): Redwood will provide one of the following options upon receipt of a legally valid request: (a) an encrypted snapshot of the runtime environment together with a signed manifest generated by Redwood's HSM containing hash-chain provenance metadata; or (b) an on-site witnessed snapshot collected in the presence of a Meridian-designated representative. Redwood will redact any Redwood proprietary telemetry prior to delivery and will produce a certificate of custody signed by Redwood's Custody Officer. Redwood's delivery timeline for option (a) shall not exceed 10 business days from request, subject to notarization and legal clearance."

Notes: we can't accept unfettered remote operator downloads of customer data; the language above limits the mechanism and creates an SLA.

2) Operator rights: replace the broad term with a defined entitlement table. Example: 
"Operator Entitlements: Diagnostics Console (read-only by default), Ephemeral SSH for debug (requires joint request and two-person approval), Audit export (WORM-compliant)."

3) Audit window: suggest a 90-day retention for high-fidelity runtime logs; production metrics kept for 365 days. We'll add an SLA for log export timelines in the SOW amendment.

Open items for Meridian: acceptance of the 10-business-day SLA for encrypted snapshot delivery or preference for on-site witnessing (we will need travel SOW if on-site). Also we need to confirm who signs off as Meridian's custody witness for chain-of-custody.

I recommend a call with Amit + our infra security lead (David) — Marissa suggested 10am PT; that works for us.

Laura Bennett

Laura / Marissa —

Thanks for the proposed language, that reads much better. Two quick clarifications from Meridian Security:

• The 10 business day SLA for option (a) is acceptable, but we need an explicit acknowledgement that emergency subpoenas or incident responses will be escalated and handled on a 48-hour best-effort timeline (we're not asking for a guaranteed 48-hour SLA, just an escalation carveout).

• For chain-of-custody, we will designate our legal person (contracts@meridianmed.com) as the witness unless otherwise notified. Please confirm format of the HSM-signed manifest (hash algorithm, signature metadata) so our forensics team can validate compatibility.

Also, we need the Order Form amended to show the on-premment 'Forensics Exhibit' as an optional SOW line item with pricing for witness-on-site travel. Can you send an amendment template ahead of the call?
